deferred_source_units.source_text: Dread and bodily shuddering had come over the man, making the pain lodged in his heart plain to those who looked at him.
deferred_source_units.reason: The shared bodily trembling does not establish a sufficiently particular relationship: Onias visibly shudders over the threatened deposits, while Habakkuk describes bodily terror at the sound of the prayer of his lips. No shared event or distinctive action beyond distress was verified.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The king himself and those with him were astonished at the young man’s spirit, for he regarded his pains as nothing.
deferred_source_units.reason: Both authorities are amazed, but the young man is admired for disregarding bodily pains, whereas the council marvels at the boldness of unlettered Peter and John. The read Acts context describes threats and release, not the torture or bodily endurance that is the focus here; this broad reaction is not retained as a distinct match.

target_units.text: When they observed Peter’s and John’s boldness and realized that they were unlettered, ordinary men, they were amazed. They also recognized that they had been with Jesus.
Seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against it.
They ordered them to leave the council and conferred with one another,
saying, “What should we do with these men? That a notable sign has taken place through them is evident to everyone living in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us warn them with threats not to speak to anyone in this name again.”
They called them in and ordered them neither to speak nor to teach at all in the name of Jesus.
Peter and John answered them, “Judge whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God;
for we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
After further threats, they released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, since everyone was glorifying God for what had happened.

records.text: Dread and bodily shuddering had come over the man, making the pain lodged in his heart plain to those who looked at him.
The king himself and those with him were astonished at the young man’s spirit, for he regarded his pains as nothing.

I kept watch, and my belly was terrified at the sound of the prayer of my lips. Trembling entered my bones, and my bodily condition beneath me was troubled. I will rest on a day of affliction, to go up to the people of my sojourning.

They called them in and ordered them neither to speak nor to teach at all in the name of Jesus.
Peter and John answered them, “Judge whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God;
for we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
After further threats, they released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, since everyone was glorifying God for what had happened.
